meta.title: Global Gas & LNG Flow Intelligence Dashboard
meta.week_convention: Weeks run Monday-Sunday; week_ending is always the Sunday, with data captured up to the 09:00 Europe/Nicosia (Cyprus time) cutoff that Sunday morning.
meta.note: Built from free/public sources (IGU World LNG Report 2026, EIA, IEA, Gas Infrastructure Europe/AGSI, operator statements, Reuters/Al Jazeera/Bloomberg/OilPrice/LNG Prime/Natural Gas Intel reporting) plus a seed infrastructure database. No live Kpler/Vortexa/ICIS feed is connected. Country-level `approximate_current_production` figures are an EI Statistical Review-class ANNUAL BASELINE (bcm/year, ~2023-25 vintage) shown for scale only — they are not a confirmed current-week production reading; do not read them as this week's output. Every flow, disruption, and storage figure carries its own confidence tag — see the Data & Method tab.

disruptions.actual_flow_affected: Force majeure declared on China/Italy/Belgium/South Korea contracts, extended repeatedly and now confirmed running into early November 2026
disruptions.description: Missile strikes on 18-19 Mar 2026 damaged two of QatarEnergy's 14 liquefaction trains at Ras Laffan (plus at least one associated Pearl GTL train, hitting condensate/LPG/naphtha/sulfur/helium byproducts). QatarEnergy estimates 3-5 years to repair. This is distinct from the Hormuz transit blockage (see separate entry): loading capacity at Ras Laffan is itself reduced by the train damage, on top of — not instead of — the transit chokepoint. Force majeure notices have now been extended into early November for European and Asian buyers; Edison (Italy) alone has had 29 cargoes (~3.8 bcm) affected since April, of which 21 were replaced from other sources. Technip Energies has since mobilised a dedicated repair team to Ras Laffan to begin work on the two damaged trains (CEO Arnaud Pieton confirmed the mobilisation); QatarEnergy's 3-5 year repair estimate stands and no revised completion date has been disclosed.
disruptions.source: LNG Industry (20 Mar 2026); The National (14 Sep 2026); Euronews (8 Sep 2026, 31 Aug 2026); Gulf International Forum / LNG Prime (Technip Energies mobilisation, 2026)

disruptions.estimated_capacity_affected: ~20 mb/d oil-equivalent normal transit; effectively all Qatari/Emirati LNG exports
disruptions.actual_flow_affected: Still a fraction of normal, but the first confirmed transits since the standstill began in early Jul 2026: a Ras-Laffan-loaded tanker (departed late Aug) reached the Gulf of Oman via Hormuz (untracked mid-transit, consistent with known jamming/interference), a stranded cargo reached Pakistan via Hormuz (~9 Sep), and 2 further LNG carriers conducted ship-to-ship transfers off Oman the week of 18 Sep
disruptions.status: Critical / ongoing — tentative signs of easing
disruptions.description: The 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis (US/Israel strikes on Iran from 28 Feb 2026, Iranian closure/mining threats, naval blockade, further escalation 5-6 Sep 2026) has made Hormuz transit the binding constraint on Qatari and Emirati LNG exports — more severe than the Ras Laffan train damage itself. A brief recovery followed a June 2026 US-Iran memorandum, but renewed attacks again halted safe passage; Tehran has since declared a restricted zone outside Hormuz. Ship-to-ship transfers off Oman (outside the strait) are now used to avoid direct transit — documented August 2026 cases include Al Rekayyat-to-Tembek (bound for India), GasLog Shanghai-to-GasLog Savannah (Asia), and Mraweh-to-LNG Enugu (Japan) — each costing $1M+ and 30-35 hours. War-risk insurance has risen from ~0.25% to 3-10% of hull value. As of 7 Sep 2026, Qatar had ~15 LNG carriers idled behind Hormuz, only 2 loading at Ras Laffan, and was repositioning 6 empty carriers toward the Gulf of Oman in what Bloomberg described as a possible partial export pivot; two empty tankers that attempted the strait itself turned back. India (~75% Hormuz-dependent LNG), Pakistan (~87%) and Bangladesh (~71%) are the most exposed importers. Qatar posted a record 21.2bn riyal ($5.8bn) Q2 2026 budget deficit, its widest since 2016, largely attributed to the export collapse. Update (18 Sep 2026): Bloomberg/Rigzone reported at least 2 LNG shipments transited Hormuz the week of 14-18 Sep as producers push to restore flows — a tanker that loaded at Ras Laffan in late August surfaced in the Gulf of Oman having evidently crossed the strait, and a separate stranded cargo reached Pakistan via Hormuz around 9 Sep, described as a 'lifeline' shipment. Two more carriers were seen doing ship-to-ship transfers off Oman the same week. Exports remain a trickle relative to the pre-crisis ~509 cargoes/half-year baseline, and Bloomberg cautions the pattern could reverse, but this is the first sourced sign of easing since the standstill that followed the Al Rekayyat attack (7 Jul 2026) and the GasLog Shanghai attack (~1 Aug 2026).
disruptions.source: Euronews (8 Sep 2026, 31 Aug 2026); The National (14 Sep 2026, 17 Jul 2026); Bloomberg/Energy Connects (7 Sep 2026, Sept 2026); Bloomberg (18 Sep 2026, 9 Sep 2026); Rigzone (18 Sep 2026)

disruptions.description: Nord Stream 1's both lines and Nord Stream 2's Line B were destroyed by sabotage in the Baltic Sea in September 2022. Nord Stream 2's Line A survived largely intact and reportedly remains pressurised/filled with gas, but has never been authorised to flow — a US investor was reported in acquisition talks as of March 2026. All four lines across both pipelines remain non-flowing as of September 2026.

disruptions.expected_restart: Confirmed for NWS and Wheatstone; unconfirmed for Gorgon
disruptions.description: Cyclone Narelle knocked out feedgas/liquefaction simultaneously across three of Australia's largest LNG complexes in late March 2026 — one headline cited 44% of Western Australian gas supply shut at the peak. This cycle's research found dated confirmation that Woodside's North West Shelf was back online by 1 Apr 2026 (workforce remobilised to offshore facilities) and that Chevron's Wheatstone resumed full production by 23 Apr 2026. Woodside's Q2 2026 results (29 Jul 2026) subsequently attributed continued NWS output softness to structural/maturing-asset decline rather than residual cyclone damage. No dated 2026 restart confirmation was found specifically for Gorgon — this remains a genuine data gap, downgraded from 'unconfirmed for all three plants' to 'unconfirmed for Gorgon only' this cycle.
disruptions.source: Bloomberg (1 Apr 2026, via search); LNG Prime/EnergyNow/Gurufocus (23 Apr 2026); Woodside Q2 2026 results (29 Jul 2026); Hydrocarbon Processing (27 Mar 2026)

disruptions.description: The Hilli Episeyo floating LNG vessel disconnected and left Cameroon around 19 Aug 2026 after 8 years of operation, heading to Singapore for upgrades before redeployment to Argentina by mid-2027. Cameroon has no replacement export unit in place, effectively stranding its offshore gas feedstock.

disruptions.actual_flow_affected: Fire on two moored FSRUs; terminal itself unaffected
disruptions.description: A drone strike on 29 Jul 2026 caused a fire on two vessels (the US FSRU Energos Winter and Greek Gaslog Salem) moored at Damietta port, suspected regional-war spillover; the Port Authority confirmed the terminal itself remained fully operational throughout.

disruptions.expected_restart: ~2 months / up to 50 days (originally targeted late Jul 2026)
disruptions.description: Train 4 was taken offline for planned maintenance from around 27 May 2026 for an approximately 2-month (up to 50-day) window; NGC's chairman confirmed no operational fault, purely scheduled work. Occurred against an already-tight global LNG market following the Qatar disruption. This cycle's search again found no dated source confirming an actual restart, so the maintenance-window status is carried forward rather than assumed resolved.
An equipment leak took Trains 1 and 5 offline around 26 May 2026; Petronas expected restart around 27 May 2026 — a short outage, not a structural one.

disruptions.estimated_capacity_affected: Reported periodic losses of up to 40% of domestic gas production during intense strike periods
disruptions.description: Russian strikes on Ukrainian gas extraction and storage infrastructure have recurred through 2026 (including large attacks reported in early Sept 2026), at times cutting domestic production by up to 40% and pushing Ukraine's own import needs higher — a demand-side drag on the wider European gas balance that compounds, rather than offsets, the EU storage shortfall below.

disruptions.location: Multiple national facilities across the EU
disruptions.estimated_capacity_affected: EU storage target cut from 90% to 80% of capacity
disruptions.actual_flow_affected: 60.8% full as of 15 Aug 2026 — weakest seasonal position since 2009
disruptions.description: EU gas storage crossed 60% on 13 Aug 2026, the weakest seasonal position since 2009, driven by LNG imports down 4.1% year-on-year and market backwardation discouraging injections. Analysts project only ~75% by end-October and say even reaching 70%+ by November will be difficult. No fresher dated AGSI+ reading found this cycle.
disruptions.source: S&P Global / Gas Infrastructure Europe (17 Aug 2026)

disruptions.estimated_capacity_affected: Slot restrictions to 34 transits/day at 50-ft draft (Sept 2026)
disruptions.actual_flow_affected: LNG-carrier transits structurally lagging even where water levels improve
disruptions.description: Drought conditions returned in early September 2026, reviving daily slot-management restrictions after an easier stretch earlier in the year. Separately, LNG-carrier transits have not rebounded even when water constraints eased, because long-term charter commitments locked many vessels into Cape-of-Good-Hope routing during the 2023-24 drought years.

Poland's segment of the Yamal-Europe pipeline is being formally absorbed into the national gas grid from around 15 September 2026, closing out its Russian-transit role — Poland now sources via Baltic Pipe (Norway) and the Świnoujście LNG terminal instead.

disruptions.actual_flow_affected: Construction/security activity resuming after years-long suspension
disruptions.description: TotalEnergies announced a full restart of all onshore and offshore activity at the long-suspended Afungi LNG project in 2026, describing it as a fresh multi-billion-dollar commitment after the multi-year insurgency-linked force majeure since 2021. Exact restart date and first-LNG timeline not independently confirmed.

disruptions.asset: LNG carrier Vivit Africa LNG (Cameron LNG cargo)
disruptions.estimated_capacity_affected: One LNG cargo (South Korean-owned Vivit Africa LNG, operated by H-Line Shipping) loaded at Cameron LNG, Louisiana
disruptions.actual_flow_affected: Cargo delivery to Rovigo, Italy suspended; vessel idled off the Italian coast then reversed course toward Algeciras, Spain instead of unloading
disruptions.expected_restart: Unresolved — cargo's onward delivery plan unclear
disruptions.description: Crew aboard the Vivit Africa LNG lost access to some internal control systems (monitoring cargo parameters) while transiting the Mediterranean and Adriatic Seas en route to Rovigo, Italy, in early September 2026, in an incident suspected — but not confirmed — to be a cyberattack. The Italian Coast Guard assisted; the vessel's Kongsberg Maritime systems vendor said it was too early to draw conclusions on cause. Rather than deliver, the vessel reversed course toward Algeciras, Spain around 16-18 Sep. This is reported as the third such tanker cyber-incident in about a month, following two oil/gas tankers boarded by the US Coast Guard and FBI off the US coast in late August over suspected cyberattacks; US officials are said to be monitoring roughly 20 vessels worldwide for similar threats. No link to a specific state or group has been confirmed. Distinct from the Damietta drone-strike incident (separate entry) — this is a suspected cyber, not kinetic, event.
disruptions.source: Bloomberg (18 Sep 2026); gCaptain/Insurance Journal (18 Sep 2026); Claims Journal (19 Sep 2026)

tenders.note: Edison confirmed QatarEnergy's force majeure on Adriatic LNG deliveries now runs into early November 2026, with 5 additional cargoes affected between late September and early November. Cumulatively, 29 of Edison's contracted cargoes have been hit since April 2026 (~3.8 bcm), of which 21 have been replaced from other sources; Edison says it can still meet customer commitments. QatarEnergy has also reportedly extended cancellations into October for Pakistani buyers and beyond September for Bangladesh.

Poland's gas mix has shifted decisively to Norwegian pipeline gas (Baltic Pipe) and LNG (Świnoujście terminal) as the Yamal-Europe route's Russian-transit role formally ended in mid-September 2026.

change_log.scope: Australia — North West Shelf & Wheatstone LNG
change_log.summary: Upgraded NWS and Wheatstone from Amber (recovery unconfirmed) to Green (restart confirmed); Gorgon remains Amber
change_log.detail: Found dated sourcing this cycle confirming Woodside's North West Shelf was back online by 1 Apr 2026 and Chevron's Wheatstone resumed full production by 23 Apr 2026, both following Cyclone Narelle repairs. No dated 2026 restart confirmation was found for Gorgon specifically, so it remains Amber as a genuine data gap. Also reclassified Pluto LNG from Green to Amber — Woodside's Q2 2026 report disclosed scheduled Train 1 cryogenic maintenance (unrelated to the cyclone) plus Scarborough/Train 2 at ~98% complete, first cargo targeted Q4 2026.
change_log.source: LNG Prime/EnergyNow/Gurufocus (23 Apr 2026); Woodside Q2 2026 results (29 Jul 2026)

change_log.summary: Force majeure extended into early November 2026; new quarterly export-collapse figure and empty-ship repositioning added
change_log.detail: QatarEnergy's force majeure on Edison's Adriatic LNG deliveries (and reportedly on other European and Asian buyers, including Pakistan into October and Bangladesh beyond September) now runs into early November 2026 — previously tracked as 'into October'. Edison has had 29 cargoes affected since April (~3.8 bcm), 21 replaced. Added a HIGH-confidence quarterly figure: Qatar's LNG exports fell from ~20 Mt/quarter (2025 baseline) to under 2 Mt in Q2 2026, alongside a record $5.8bn quarterly budget deficit. Also added detail that Qatar is repositioning empty carriers (6 toward the Gulf of Oman as of 7 Sep) while only 2 vessels load at Ras Laffan and ~15 remain idled behind Hormuz — described by Bloomberg as a possible partial export pivot, though two ships that attempted the strait itself turned back.
change_log.source: Euronews (31 Aug 2026, 8 Sep 2026); Bloomberg/Energy Connects (7 Sep 2026, Sept 2026); The National (14 Sep 2026)

change_log.summary: First sourced signs of partial Hormuz transit resumption since the Jul 2026 standstill
change_log.detail: Bloomberg/Rigzone (18 Sep 2026) reported at least 2 LNG shipments transiting Hormuz the week of 14-18 Sep, plus a stranded cargo reaching Pakistan via Hormuz around 9 Sep and 2 further carriers doing ship-to-ship transfers off Oman. Volumes remain a small fraction of the pre-crisis baseline and the trend could reverse, but this is the first easing signal tracked since the standstill following the Al Rekayyat (7 Jul) and GasLog Shanghai (~1 Aug) tanker attacks.

change_log.summary: Technip Energies confirmed mobilised to begin physical repair work on the damaged trains
change_log.detail: CEO Arnaud Pieton confirmed Technip Energies has mobilised a dedicated team to Ras Laffan for repair work on Trains 4 & 6. QatarEnergy's 3-5 year repair estimate is unchanged and no revised completion date has been disclosed.
